name: Snake River Campground
note: A rustic Aitkin County Land Department campground in county forest on the Snake River off State Highway 65, about 6 miles south of McGrath. It connects to the Redtop and Soo Line ATV trails, so expect ATV traffic. Pad size is not posted; the county's site photos show open gravel and grass spurs. Creekside on site 10 (and likely 12), on an open lawn at the river bank; the other sites sit behind trees. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Aitkin County Land Department pages (land-campgrounds.php and land-campground-snake-river.php, read 2026-11-12): one of 'four campgrounds' the department manages; 'Snake River Campground, South of McGrath, On the Snake River, $20/night, Primitive, 12 sites'; '12 campsites, pit toilets, drinking water, picnic tables, canoe landing, but no electricity'; 'Camping: $20.00 per night per site'; address 10890 State Hwy 65, McGrath; GPS 46°10'12"N 93°15'33"W. Reservations through the county's OneGov portal (permit=4, 'Snake River Park', '12 sites, $20.00 per night'). The county campground map (img/SnakeRiverCampground.jpg, 2011 county GIS) draws a road along the river with sites 1-10, a loop with 11-12, self-registration, hand pump, pit toilet, canoe landing and ATV/hiking trails; the site-photo PDF (pdf/SnakeRiver.pdf, 2016) shows every site as an open gravel/grass drive-in spur among scattered trees, several clearly long enough for a 23-ft rig. Esri World Imagery 2025-09-28 (WV02, rendered at 600 m, 220 m, z18 and z19) shows the gravel road and loop matching the map at 46.1700,-93.2590, and Wayback 2011-05-16 shows a vehicle on the loop. A real drive-in county campground with a posted nightly rate (public: no price gate). Not 5445 Snake River Campground - Chengwatana State Forest (45.8226,-92.7804), which is ~53 km SE in Pine County; nearest DB entry is 5373 Father Hennepin State Park, 18 km.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12: Esri World Imagery 2025-09-28 (WV02 0.5 m; export at 600 m and 220 m, z18 and z19 3x3 stitches, all rendered) plus Wayback 2011-05-16 (UC-G 0.3 m, z19, rendered). The river road carrying sites 1-9 runs ~35-45 m from the Snake River behind a continuous wooded belt (no on-water value for those). At the SE end of the road, just before the loop, one open mown lawn runs from the road edge (~46.16974,-93.25834) to the south bank (~46.17002,-93.25793 to 46.17003,-93.25804) with only scattered trees and a thin brushy fringe at the bank; the 2011 frame shows a picnic table at ~46.16984,-93.25789, ~19 m from the water across open grass, and the boulders lining the lawn that the county's site photos show. The county site-photo PDF (2016) frames site 10's post, table and fire ring on that lawn with the river and reeds directly behind, and its 'Site 10 and 12' photo shows tents on the same open grass; the county map puts 10 and 12 on the river side at the road's SE end. River width measured at the lawn on the z19 frames: ~20-29 m perpendicular (a gravel bar splits it just upstream), under the ~30 m line -> creekside, not riverfront. Free-flowing river, no dam. Only sites 10 (and likely 12) qualify; the rest are behind trees.

fees.note: Per site per night. The county accepts Visa, Mastercard and Discover; the card processor adds a fee.

booking.note: Online reservations must be made at least 7 days before arrival; after that, first come, first served with a self-registration station.

booking_source: https://www.aitkincountymn.gov/departments/land/land-campgrounds.php ('Reservations are made online and must be made no later than 7 days in advance of your stay. After that, it is first-come, first-served camping.') + county map (self-registration station), read 2026-11-12

sites_source: county Snake River page ('There are 12 campsites') + land-campgrounds.php ('12 sites') + county map (sites 1-12), read 2026-11-12
facilities_source: county Snake River page ('pit toilets, drinking water, picnic tables, canoe landing') + OneGov notes ('drinking water (hand pump)'), read 2026-11-12
flags: Waterfront: creekside rests on site 10 (and probably 12) on the one open lawn at the road's SE end, tied to the number by the county's 2016 site photo and its schematic 2011 map; sites 1-9 sit behind a wooded belt. River measured ~20-29 m wide, so creekside rather than riverfront.

Rig fit: the county gives no length; its 2016 site photos show open gravel/grass spurs, several plainly long enough for a 23-ft rig. Kept with the pad-size caveat (AWH 2026-11-02). No agency statement about a road problem; the address is on State Hwy 65.
ATV trails (Redtop, Soo Line) connect to the campground: a general county campground with an OHV side, not an OHV staging camp; caveat in the note.

Season not stated by the county (it says only that snow is not plowed at any campground; aggregators say May-late October); left absent. The county's water on/off dates name only Aitkin and Berglund parks.
Pin 46.17008,-93.25896 is on the river road among the sites (county GPS 46.1700,-93.2592 falls ~60 m W on the same road). Elevation from Open-Meteo at the pin.
Phone is the Aitkin County Land Department (218-927-7364), the number on the campground page.
Duplicate check: no 'Snake River' entry in MN except 5445 (Chengwatana State Forest, ~53 km SE, Pine County); nothing else within 18 km.
